chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Don Byas and Ben Webster: cutting contests at the bar
summary: Both part Indian from the Southwest, Byas would wait for Webster to drink too much before coming in to cut him.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: What was Don Byas like as a person?
Beautiful, that's all I can say. You know, he was -- the same thing like Ben, he was a wahoo, the Indian in him.
Yeah. And Don was from Oklahoma and Ben was around Texas and Oklahoma. All of them were around the same part of the country, you know?
And they were great friends, weren't they?
And you were telling me off the tape, earlier, about cutting contests they used to have.
Yeah. Oh, the one that I think I spoke about was a recording -- no, this wasn't Don on this.
You were telling me about a cutting contest where Don would stand in the --
Oh, would stand in the back.
At the end of the bar and wait till Ben

had one too many. Because when Ben was all right he was right. They were both great, you know, but he would wait till Ben would go off his rocker, after he'd had a couple of tastes or something. Then he would pick up his horn and come in, you know, and Ben couldn't even walk. He would just stand up there and hold his horn in his hands, and Don was in good shape, you know.
